extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders in the National Apprenticeship System (program sponsors, employers, State Apprenticeship Agencies, Office of Apprenticeship, intermediaries, educational institutions, and regulated community)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of proposed definitions and related program metric definitions in the DOL NPRM revising 29 CFR part 29; intended to clarify terms used for registration, program design, performance measurement, and roles within the National Apprenticeship System. Useful for stakeholders preparing comments or ensuring compliance with proposed rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: cohort completion rate (context of fiscal year calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies existing practice of calculating the cohort completion rate on a fiscal year basis to enable more consistent data reporting; explains when an apprentice will not be included in the calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation seeks to provide clarity on calculating cohort completion rate on a fiscal year basis; invites comment on this proposed definition. Related to proposed §§29.25 (performance measures) and fiscal year definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: collective bargaining agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as the written agreement between an employer (or a group of employers) and the bargaining representative(s) of a labor union to which employees of the employer(s) belong that addresses such topics as wages, hours, workplace health and safety, employee benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, collective bargaining agreements inform development of registered apprenticeship program standards and typically govern an employer's participation in a group program. Department invites comments to increase clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Attainment of knowledge, skills, and abilities specified in a work process schedule; removes phrase 'manual, mechanical or technical skills and knowledge' to align with competency frameworks (e.g., O*NET, DOL competency models). Includes measurable attainment of techniques as a qualifier for hands-on practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns regulatory definition with industry-recognized competency frameworks used to develop work process schedules (§29.7(b)). Emphasizes inclusion of 'techniques' (physical use of equipment/tools) as measurable attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: corrective action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Product that must be produced when a State Apprenticeship Plan is not granted full approval by the Department (as described in proposed §29.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide SAAs with clear actions needed to be eligible for full approval of the State Apprenticeship Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: credential rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of registered apprenticeship program completers in a cohort that receive an interim credential (interim credential defined separately); excludes Certificates of Completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to incentivize leveraging recognized postsecondary credentials (including industry-recognized credentials) into program design and to drive portability and national recognition. Programs not required to offer interim credentials; Department acknowledges some industries may not issue interim credentials and does not intend this as a sole indicator of program quality. Proposes excluding apprentices who leave during the probationary period from this measure; seeks comment on whether probationary leavers should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprentice
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant at least 16 years of age (unless higher minimum age fixed by law) in a registered CTE apprenticeship program covered by subpart B and part 30; aligned with 'apprentice' in subpart A but distinct for purposes of certain regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly states minimum age may be higher where required by law; clarifies that a CTE apprentice is not an apprentice for purposes of listed CFR provisions (29 CFR 4.6(p), 5.2, 5.5(a)(4), and 570.50(b)). Primary purpose is to differentiate models and ensure clarity for regulated community.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A written agreement that complies with proposed §29.24 and contains terms and conditions for employment and training of the CTE apprentice; differentiates from subpart A apprenticeship agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements largely follow proposed §29.9 with minor differences reflecting registered CTE apprenticeship model (e.g., shorter maximum probationary period).

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship-related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Organized and systematic instruction that provides a CTE apprentice with knowledge of theoretical and technical subjects related to an approved industry skills framework; required to be delivered through a State-approved CTE program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor may prescribe additional coursework (including outside program). Instruction may be classroom, electronic media, or other State CTE Agency/Registration Agency approved forms. Distinguishes from 'related instruction' in subpart A, which does not require a State-approved CTE program.

rubrics_metrics.name: day (calendar day)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage of 'day' throughout proposed rule and 29 CFR part 30 means calendar day, not business day or workday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies meaning to remove ambiguity where 'day' is used in the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains existing definition referring to the Department of Labor (DOL) used throughout the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive change; term continues to refer to DOL in the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: direct threat
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'direct threat' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carried over for consistency with EEO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'disability' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with EEO definitions used elsewhere in DOL regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'EEO' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent reference to equal employment opportunity within apprenticeship regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: electronic media
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifies definition to remove specific examples because technology evolves rapidly; contemporary examples include interactive mapping/databases, editing/transmitting digital files, chat/video conferencing participation, and accessing documents via enterprise document-sharing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed are non-exhaustive; removal of static examples prevents rapid obsolescence of regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: employer (in relation to apprentices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity that employs an apprentice during the on-the-job training component and provides apprentice training under an approved set of standards and apprenticeship agreement; applies to employment of apprentices under subparts A, B, and C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies dual usage of 'employer' (general term and employer-of-apprentice), ensures entities understand role during on-the-job training and obligations under program standards; aims to assure apprentices that employers will abide by on-the-job training requirements and program standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'ethnicity' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For consistency with EEO reporting and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: exit (for performance measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exit is when an apprentice has ended participation in a registered apprenticeship program; includes apprentices who completed the program or who have canceled or been canceled from the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed inclusion of these groups together ensures accurate measurement of outcomes after the probationary period for measures like annual completion rate, cohort completion rate, and credential rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal purposes (registered apprenticeship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revises definition by adding 'registered' before 'apprenticeship' to clarify that 'apprenticeship' means 'registered apprenticeship' unless stated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that registration in the National Apprenticeship System overseen by OA conveys authority and may trigger benefits/obligations under Federal laws (e.g., Davis-Bacon, IRA, WIOA).

rubrics_metrics.name: fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines fiscal year as the Federal Government accounting period covering October 1 through September 30; the fiscal year is named by the calendar year in which the period ends (e.g., Oct 1, 2022–Sept 30, 2023 is fiscal year 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed use to set parameters around 'annual completion rate' and 'cohort completion rate' measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: genetic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'genetic information' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For consistency with EEO and nondiscrimination provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: group program
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsored and registered by an organization that develops a set of registered apprenticeship program standards that are adopted contractually by one or more participating employers (typically via collective bargaining or program standards adoption agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines widely-used informal term to formal regulatory term; clarifies how sponsors and participating employers adopt and implement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: industry skills framework
rubrics_metrics.description: New term to establish concept of an industry skills framework for development of an on-the-job training outline, distinct component of standards for registered CTE apprenticeship under subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to guide development of OJT outlines and align training to approved industry frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: institution of higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds definition from the Higher Education Act of 1965; identifies institutions of higher education as eligible program sponsors of registered CTE apprenticeships (per proposed §29.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns definition across statutes to provide consistency for regulated community.

rubrics_metrics.name: interim credential
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified to specify that an interim credential is a recognized postsecondary credential and documentation of attainment of competency milestones within an occupation suitable for registered apprenticeship training; usually part of a career pathway and standalone recognized postsecondary credential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with ETA's definition under WIOA for measuring credential attainment. Interim credentials may be issued by sponsor, related instruction provider, employer, or industry intermediary and used to document competency attainment or measurable skill gain as part of a work process schedule (§29.8(a)(8)). Excludes Certificate of Completion from the 'credential rate' metric; may be stacked or portable across industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: intermediary
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity that assists in provision or coordination of a registered apprenticeship program or otherwise provides support to a registered apprenticeship program (e.g., industry vetting of training, establishing networks/partnerships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes intermediaries' role while clarifying they do not assume responsibilities reserved for Registration Agencies (SAAs and OA), such as final determinations on occupation suitability or final program approval. Examples include labor organizations, trade organizations, industry experts. Department welcomes comment to refine this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: journeyworker
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to emphasize 'experienced' worker who is proficient in skills and competencies necessary to be successful in an industry or occupation; replaces prior language about 'attained a level of skill...mastered' with 'proficient'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes level of experience to gain proficiency differs by industry. 'Proficiency' intended to capture mastery necessary to transfer skills to apprentices. Encourages commenters to identify if industry proficiency suffices or occupational proficiency must be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly defined; central concept capturing extent of an individual's mastery or expertise with respect to critical job skills and competencies necessary to train apprentices effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout the regulations to describe journeyworker capability and apprentices' success in careers pursued through registered apprenticeship. Provides rationale with examples (e.g., trades completing tasks efficiently and safely).

rubrics_metrics.name: local educational agency (LEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds definition from the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965; identifies LEAs as eligible program sponsors of registered CTE apprenticeships (per proposed §29.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns definition for consistency and clarity for regulated community.

rubrics_metrics.name: local registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines registration of an apprenticeship program for Federal purposes by a Registration Agency within a particular State; occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship may be eligible for local registration consistent with approved work process schedule and related instruction outline (§29.7(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between locally registered programs and nationally registered programs; both confer Federal registration benefits, but national programs and local registration have separate criteria (see proposed §29.14 and §29.15(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: major life activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition of 'major life activities' from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included for consistency with EEO and disability-related protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Apprenticeship System
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the full scope of stakeholders involved with maintaining and supporting registered apprenticeship in the United States, including OA, SAAs, employers, labor unions, business organizations, trade/industry groups, educational institutions, intermediaries, and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe the coordinated efforts of Department and stakeholders; clarifies which entities are included when references are made to the national system.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition for templates of registered apprenticeship program standards developed by a national-scope entity (e.g., labor union, trade association), recognized by OA and adapted for local registration; proposed §29.15 would establish criteria/process for recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains relation to National Occupational Standards and National Program Standards; Department proposes recognition process and invites comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: New definition for a product to support development of registered apprenticeship programs across traditional and emerging industries; intended to be tailored to specific occupations and adopted by programs as the Department develops them (§29.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department commits to robust process to ensure standards are relevant to industry and would require sponsors to adopt them as they become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards for Apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines registered program standards developed by a program sponsor for nationwide, reciprocal registration by OA; proposed §29.14 would establish criteria and process for registration on a nationwide basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished from National Guidelines (templates adapted locally) and tied to OA's national registration processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: non-compete clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Term in apprenticeship agreement or other agreement between an employer or sponsor and an apprentice that prohibits the apprentice from seeking or accepting employment with another employer during the registered apprenticeship program or registered CTE apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition clarifies the scope of restrictive terms in apprenticeship agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Apprenticeship (OA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Largely retains existing definition but adds reference to Secretary's designation of National Apprenticeship System oversight to ETA and OA; capitalizes 'Apprenticeship' to align with OA's official title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor updates to reflect oversight responsibilities within DOL.

rubrics_metrics.name: on-the-job training
rubrics_metrics.description: Organized and systematic training conducted at a workplace/jobsite designed to provide hands-on knowledge, skills, techniques, and competencies necessary to achieve proficiency in an occupation suitable for registered apprenticeship; distinguished from 'related instruction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires apprentices to be paid wages based on wage progression schedule in approved standards or collective bargaining agreement while contributing to employer productivity. Related instruction described separately (classroom/electronic/self-study) with proposed minimum of average 144 hours per 2,000 OJT hours under §29.7(b)(4). Registered CTE apprenticeship under subpart B will require minimum 540 hours of CTE apprenticeship-related instruction (encompassing at least 12 postsecondary credit hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: participating employer
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer that does not act as program sponsor but agrees (via collective bargaining joint committee sponsor or program standards adoption agreement) to adopt sponsor's standards and serve as employer of record for program apprentices, paying wages and providing closely supervised OJT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to hold participating employers accountable for meeting requirements in this part and 29 CFR part 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: physical or mental impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds the existing definition from 29 CFR part 30 into §29.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included for consistency with EEO/disability protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: pre-apprenticeship program
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition added to part 29; retains many aspects of 29 CFR part 30 definition but aligns with WIOA (20 CFR 681.480) and ILO Recommendation No. 208; includes elements regarding access to educational/career counseling, supportive services, and opportunities to earn industry-recognized credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to usages in parts 29 and 30; individuals in pre-apprenticeship are not 'apprentices' under these regulations. Proposed §29.25 would authorize collection of information from sponsors about pre-apprenticeship programs and apprentices recruited from them. Emphasizes equitable, intentional, achievable strategies to recruit/retain individuals from underserved communities and alignment with non-discrimination/EEO requirements. Pre-apprenticeship, registered CTE apprenticeship, and registered apprenticeship viewed collectively as apprenticeship pathways; pre-apprenticeship activities (job shadowing, internships, etc.) can prepare CTE students for registered CTE apprenticeship.
